title: Aspect 5: Result and Completion Trigger Perfective
titleRussian: Виды глагола 5: Результат и завершение — СВ
description: Time markers that signal completion (уже, наконец, за час, к утру) trigger the perfective. Today: identifying these cues and choosing the perfective past.
descriptionRussian: Слова и фразы, выражающие завершение (уже, наконец, за час, к утру), требуют совершенного вида.
intro: The mirror image of lesson 4. Where duration and repetition pull one way, finishing pulls the other: words meaning already, finally, or at last, plus two time phrases that mean the action got done inside a span or by a deadline. Between the two lessons you now have most of the cues that turn up in real sentences.
rules: Completion adverbs (уже, наконец, сразу, быстро) trigger the perfective: the action is finished or happened as a single event.

'За + accusative time' (за час, за день, за тридцать минут) trigger the perfective: the time after 'за' is how long the action took to be COMPLETED. Compare to bare accusative duration (час, два часа), which triggers the imperfective.
'К + dative time' (к утру, к понедельнику) trigger the perfective: the action got finished BY that point in time.
examples: Я уже прочитал книгу. (I already finished the book.) Уже → СВ.
Маша наконец написала статью. (Masha finally finished the article.) Наконец → СВ.
Антон сделал работу за час. (Anton finished the work in an hour.) За + acc → СВ.
Лена выучила урок к утру. (Lena learned the lesson by morning.) К + dat → СВ.
Они быстро приготовили обед. (They quickly cooked dinner.) Быстро + completion → СВ.
Я сразу купил книгу. (I bought the book right away.) Сразу → СВ.

items.promptEnglish: As a child, Masha often read books.
items.hint: Recap from Lesson 4: 'часто' is which family of cue?
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 4: часто is a habit cue, locking the verb into the imperfective. Today's lesson covers the OPPOSITE cue family: completion / result, which forces the perfective.

items.promptEnglish: Anton has already finished the work.
items.hint: 'Уже' marks completion. Subject Антон is masculine.
items.explanation: Уже (already) signals the action is finished. Perfective сделал, masc -л. The pair is делать / сделать (prefix с-).

items.promptEnglish: Masha read the book through in an hour.
items.hint: 'За час' is a perfective time-frame cue. Subject Маша is feminine.
items.explanation: 'За час' (in an hour) measures the time the action took to be COMPLETED, locking in the perfective. Прочитала, fem -ла. Compare with the bare accusative 'час' (an hour) without 'за', which would be a duration cue and trigger the imperfective.

items.hint: 'Наконец' is a completion cue. Male speaker.
items.explanation: Наконец (finally) marks the action as finished at last. Perfective написал, masc -л. The pair is писать / написать (prefix на-).

items.promptEnglish: They learned the lesson by morning.
items.hint: 'К утру' is a deadline cue. Plural subject.
items.explanation: 'К утру' (by morning) sets a deadline by which the action got completed. Perfective выучили, plural -ли. The pair is учить / выучить (prefix вы-).

items.hint: 'Быстро' (quickly) often pairs with a single completed action. Feminine subject.
items.explanation: Быстро (quickly) here describes the speed of a single completed cooking event. Perfective приготовила, fem -ла. The pair is готовить / приготовить (prefix при-).

blanks: Они _____ работу к понедельнику. (They finished the work by Monday.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: 'К понедельнику' (by Monday) is a perfective deadline cue. Plural subject takes -ли. Сделали marks completion by the deadline.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: I (m) wrote the article in thirty minutes.
minimalPairs.explanation: 'За тридцать минут' is a 'за + acc time' phrase: it measures how long the action took to COMPLETE. Perfective написал. The bare accusative 'тридцать минут' without за would mark duration and select писал.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Masha got dinner ready by seven o'clock.
minimalPairs.explanation: 'К семи часам' (by seven o'clock) is a 'к + dat time' deadline phrase, locking in the perfective. Приготовила marks the completed result. Готовила would describe only the cooking process, with no claim of completion.

errorCorrection.sentence: Антон уже пил кофе, когда я пришёл.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Anton had already drunk his coffee when I arrived.
errorCorrection.explanation: Уже plus a second past event ('when I arrived') frames the coffee as finished before that point, which takes the perfective: выпил ('had already drunk'). Imperfective пил would describe the drinking still in progress, contradicting уже.

errorCorrection.sentence: Вчера Маша убирала квартиру за час.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Yesterday Masha cleaned the apartment in an hour.
errorCorrection.explanation: 'За час' (in an hour) is a 'за + accusative time' phrase: it measures the time taken to reach completion, which locks in the perfective убрала. Imperfective убирала describes only the process and cannot combine with the completion frame.

errorCorrection.sentence: Антон учил все слова к утру и лёг спать.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Anton had learned all the words by morning and went to bed.
errorCorrection.explanation: 'К утру' is a deadline phrase ('by morning'), and a deadline locks in the perfective: выучил marks the words fully learned by that point, matching the next completed event 'лёг спать.' Imperfective учил would leave the learning unfinished.

errorCorrection.sentence: Он долго искал ключи и наконец находил их.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: He looked for the keys a long time and finally found them.
errorCorrection.explanation: Наконец (finally) marks the achievement of a result after effort, which takes the perfective: нашёл. Imperfective находил would describe repeatedly or habitually finding ('used to find'), not the single moment of success that 'finally' names.

errorCorrection.sentence: Когда зазвонил будильник, она сразу вставала.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: When the alarm rang, she immediately got up.
errorCorrection.explanation: Сразу (right away) points to a single, instant completed reaction, which takes the perfective: встала. Imperfective вставала would describe a repeated or drawn-out getting-up ('used to get up'), not the one-time immediate response to the alarm.

errorCorrection.sentence: Маша открывала окно, и в комнате стало свежо.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Masha opened the window, and the room became fresh.
errorCorrection.explanation: A completed action that produces a result takes the perfective: открыла marks the window as actually opened, which is what makes the room fresh. Imperfective открывала describes only the process ('was opening'), without guaranteeing the window got open, so it clashes with the result clause.

reviewVocab.definition: already (completion adverb; locks the verb into the perfective)
finally, at last (completion adverb; locks the verb into the perfective)
in (a time; with accusative; measures the time it took to complete the action; locks in the perfective)
